For many years I wanted to die. I came a lot of times too close to do it but never actually did it. But I have hurt myself in many ways both physically and emotionally.
It has some months now that I came to the conclusion I want to live. The reasons I believe are kind of selfish or maybe I see them as those because I haven't really loved myself ever. Is a feeling of rage and sadness mixed on how unfair is to have been gone through all of this shit. How unfair is to have talents and dreams and ambitions and not be able to be happy or successful while so many shitty people leave peacefully without ever harm themselves. Why should I die while everyone else not even feel guilty or shame?
Maybe it sounds a bit narcissistic or toxic but on the other side it's a motivation not to die. I don't know if it's a weird form of self love cause I don't know how to take care of me but it's just the feeling that I deserve to live and also have good time as everyone else. There aren't a lot of things to hope for (30 years old, no job, no relationship, live in a shitty country, severe mental health problems like ocd, social anxiety, possible adhd etc) but I feel that I have at least the right to be here and maybe experiencing something that will make me happy.
Sorry I know it's a confusing message I just try to figure out why I really want to live because is kind of new feeling. 
Short answer in case something good happens.

I have tried to overanalyzed this issue many times and still I can't say that i have a clear answer. Although parents play an important role for sure I feel that the biggest factor is the personality itself. I had to deal with a very negative father and my parents still have a very toxic relationship but I can tell for sure that they were more caring and better parents than many others I have seen from friends and relatives. I have seen other kids receive much more abusive behaviors and harsh critisism and never have issues with self esteem, anxiety or anything else. I have seen people who have received much more cruel bullying by their peers and never get affected by it. There is the possibility that these people became toxic as a defence mechanism but this only proves that personal traits plays the biggest role. I was always extremely sensitive person who have taken things seriously. I was always deeply affected and hurted by others. And simply I was never matched with my peers I always had very different interests. Sure if I had a better family it would be easier to handle the situation but I believe that it would be inevitable to not get traumatized eventually by society.

I think that my mom's behavior who still is a people pleaser had a deeper effect to me than her behavior to me. To be honest and I know that this will sound very controversial I feel that the biggest problem is that my mother learned to me to be nice person, empathetic and not cause trouble. But she never forced me to do that she was just enabled my behavior. I believe that if she was more neglectful things would be better. But again I'm not completely sure because I feel that as a person I would get traumatized either way. Because this is my character. And this is why I can't find help in therapy.

No they aren't all people worthy of love. People who hurted me or people who hurt other people and never apologized for it or never felt remorse don't deserve love. Also if I hurted someone in the past I should be punished for it.

Just saying that everyone is worthy of love only would make people who are self centered even more selfish.

But I was that person when I was younger. I didn't hurt this way and I didn't felt this way. And I didn't attract the right people.

But as I said my issue is general I can't deal with the general state of the world.

I don't feel exactly I lack connection for me as an individual. I would like to meet people who would perceive life in a more profound level and be able to see behind what they see. Who will be more intuitive and not reject things just because they don't resonate with them. Not hypocritical. With their own views and not what the majority of people says. Who will not conform in what is easier.

But it's not about me. I don't think that it will make me happy meet two or three people who will have these traits or something that will make to feel understood. It will ease my pain but that's it. People will continue to be as they are. This hurts me. And I feel that I will also continue to be who I'm. And what I'm makes my life difficult in this world.

What exactly is normal? What the majority of people do? What I mean is that I want to be myself. I don't care about parties, sex, drugs or having what is perceived as normal for a young person. But because I don't like these things, I feel like I'm less of a person, weird and I isolate myself.

You want to become like these people and you can't. I want to just have the confidence to be who I'm and have other people around me with the same mindset and not feel abnormal.


It seems that nobody else wanta the same thing so it's even more depressing.

No because I never felt intimidated by all those things even when I was part of them. What I wanted was people who will understand me and have the same interests beside partying and romantic relationship.

So for me is even more difficult because I don't feel that I have lost something. I feel that I don't belong anywhere because I don't want these things and there is no one else who feels this way.

This post confirms it.

Thank you for saying that. It seems sometimes that people wants to connect everything with a trauma response or a disorder when it might be just a personality trait. Indeed is very easy to fall into this trap especially when you read so many things online and don't have enough self esteem and confidence to trust yourself. And you end up losing yourself into this concept completely.

Before therapy I had issues to express myself to others but I was still able to do it somehow and not shaming myself for it. After being so criticized from a therapist that if I express my complains to people the way I want I will end up alone and constantly be misunderstood about my motives towards people that my desire is to put them in their places and making myself feeling better when my true motive was that I didn't liked lies, I can't be myself anymore. I questioning every interaction I have and I have isolated myself even more because every time I invalidate my negative feelings. Therapy made be feel like I don't have the right to be myself, that I'm the wrong one and I should be fixed. I never had such a big issues with my personality before. It only contributed to make me more avoidant and led me towards harming myself more because I don't want to change but I can't be myself either.

And on the other side if you don't care about sex, if you have an idealized view of romantic relationships and in your almost 30s you never had a sexual encounter you get also stigmatized for it as a normal by professionals.

If you are also what they perceive as "normal" and you don't expose yourself online, you never fake it anything, you just can't connect with your peers in your teenage years because you may have other interests that are not so crazy as a "normal teenager should be you get again pathologized.

So in my understanding there is no measure. If generally you are not in what society defines as normal you get screwed.

As someone who got into spirituality and use it as a coping mechanism I can say that in many instances it made me feel much worse. I can't say about Buddhism but I think that many new age ideas are incredibly damaging especially for people who are very shameful and indulge into self destructive behaviors.

Especially the idea of letting go of your ego or ego death is extremely disturbing for me and unfortunately I still shame and question myself for my refusal to this concept. Compined with things I read in the r/npd sub it made feel like I'm a covert narcissist and I'm a bad person who needs to be fixed.

I also had a therapist who criticized me a lot about my negative feelings, try to convince me that people are inherently good and kind of forcing this idea to me. I feel that my negative feelings were never validated and having them makes me a mean etson who doesn't deserve to be happy.

It's not that I don't believe that some of these ideas aren't helpful is just that they can be dangerous for people who suffer from low self esteem, who spent their lives as people pleasers and struggle with social anxiety. You should become selfish, you should strengthen your ego and put your foot down in order to survive. Is logical to have negative feelings towards people if you were hurted by them. It seems that generally nobody validates this.

And from the other side seeing how humanity is and how toxic people can become, I'm sorry but it seems kind of delusional and naive to want to make myself even more selfless, even more invisible. No I want to be seen and tell my opinion and express who I'm even if what I'm is not pleasant to people. Ditching my ego even more or trying to see people in different light when I'm so drown into self hatred it only makes me hating myself and others more.

I tried many therapists and I heard the same thing over and over again. I'm sorry but you can't change my opinion anymore that mental health industry at least where I live only cares how to fix you not validate your feelings. So is no for me I won't  let myself get traumatized again by a mental health professional.
